answers.why: “God of Israel” names the God of the nation whose members seek him.
“Holy One of Israel” identifies God in relation to the nation.
The blessing praises the LORD as the nation's “God of Israel.”
Israel is described collectively as those who are pure in heart.
“In Judah” denotes the people's territory, alongside Salem and Zion.
God's name is great among Israel, parallel to his being known in Judah.
The law in Israel is entrusted to fathers to teach successive generations.
God's anger falls on the wilderness people because “they believed not.”
Israel's young men are struck down among the people eating in the wilderness.
The wilderness people provoke their God, called the “Holy One of Israel.”
God rejects Israel because of their high places and graven images.
Israel is God's inheritance whom David shepherds, parallel to “Jacob his people.”
